The cloak design problem is formulated as minimizing two antagonistic criteria: protection (C1) and invisibility (C2).
Protection criterion C1 is the normalized integral of the squared field inside the protected region.
Invisibility criterion C2 is the normalized integral of the squared difference between cloaked and free-space fields in the surrounding region.
The search space for permittivity values is either ternary discrete {7, 10, 12} or continuous in [7, 12].
The chaotic ternary grey wolf optimizer (CTGWO) is designed to handle ternary discrete search spaces with enhanced exploration.
CTGWO divides the wolf pack into exploration and exploitation groups to improve diversity and avoid premature convergence.
The grey wolf optimizer simulates social hunting behavior with three leaders (α, β, δ) guiding the search.
The parameter 'a' in GWO decreases from 2 to 0 over iterations to shift from exploration to exploitation.
The bi-objective NSGA-II algorithm uses non-dominated sorting and crowding distance to generate Pareto fronts.
Finite element method with second order Lagrange elements is used to solve the 2D scalar Helmholtz equation.
The cloak and protected regions are meshed with triangle elements of size λ/12 and λ/6 respectively, with λ=500 nm.
The study focuses on transverse magnetic (TM) polarization where permittivity is the inverse of σ in the Helmholtz equation.
The cloak design avoids geometric transforms, differing from classical transformation optics approaches.
Previous works used topology optimization and genetic algorithms with fewer parameters; this work optimizes a much larger parameter set.
The paper demonstrates that CTGWO outperforms comparative mono-objective algorithms in convergence and solution quality.
Bi-objective optimization provides a set of trade-off solutions rather than a single optimum, useful for user preference.
The cloaking problem is mathematically equivalent for electromagnetic, acoustic, and anti-plane shear waves under certain conditions.
Perfectly Matched Layers (PMLs) are used to simulate unbounded free space in numerical simulations.
The study uses a scalar scattering model with permittivity and permeability as scalar fields in the TM case.
The ternary update rules in CTGWO use modulo operations to keep contributions within [0,2].
The paper includes a detailed mathematical formulation of GWO and NSGA-II algorithms adapted for the cloak design problem.
